raw_segments.text: Someone called to him to put on his hat as it was cold, but he flung the hat in the snow
as though he were angry and kept repeating,
I won't have the hat, I won't have the hat.
Smurov picked it up and carried it after him.
All the boys were crying, and Kalia and the boy who discovered about Troy most of all.
Though Smurov, with the captain's hat in his hand, was crying bitterly too, he managed,
as he ran, to snatch up a piece of red brick that lay on the snow of the path, to fling
it at the flock of sparrows that was flying by.
He missed them, of course, and went on crying as he ran.
Halfway, Snegaryov suddenly stopped, stood still for half a minute, as though struck
by something and suddenly turning back to the church ran towards the deserted grave.
But the boys instantly overtook him and caught hold of him on all sides.
Then he fell helpless on the snow as though he had been knocked down, and struggling,
sobbing and wailing, he began crying out,
Elisha, old man, dear old man.
Alyosha and Kalia tried to make him get up, soothing and persuading him.
